game.title: Alone in the Dark
game.blurb: Psychological survival horror set in the 1920s American South, a reimagining of the original Alone in the Dark, from Pieces Interactive, released 2024-03-20. RAWG has no playtime yet. Genres: Action, Adventure. Chapters are an estimate drawn from Steam achievement themes.

chapters.title: Derceto Manor and Beyond
chapters.summary: The story of Edward Carnby and Emily Hartwood at Derceto Manor, with its many hidden milestones. Spoiler-guarded.

chapters.title: Monsters and Weapons
chapters.summary: Melee, ranged, fire, shotgun and opportunity kills, and breaking through barriers.

chapters.title: Lagniappes, Clues and Safes
chapters.summary: Finishing Lagniappe sets, finding them all, reading every clue and opening every safe and lock.

chapters.title: Completion Challenges
chapters.summary: Finishing without drinking from the flask, and earning every achievement.

notes: Backlog game, all-AAA pass: picked from RAWG's most-added list for its year across all genres (docs/PLAN.md section 2, genre filter widened 2026-10-23). This is the 2024 remake; RAWG describes it as a "reimagination of the classic survival horror game". RAWG's entry uses the slug "alone-in-the-dark-2022" (id 849517) but gives the 2024-03-20 release date. It uses the remake's own Steam app, 1310410 ("Alone in the Dark"); app 1938800 is a separate "Alone in the Dark Prologue", and the older games have their own apps. No StrategyWiki page under "Alone in the Dark (2024)" or "Alone in the Dark (2023)". aloneinthedark.fandom.com answers under "Alone in the Dark (2024)" ("Alone in the Dark (2023)" redirects there), with about 21 linked pages, including "Edward Carnby (2023)", "Emily Hartwood (2023)", "Lagniappes" and "Easter Eggs in Alone in the Dark (2024)"; names only were looked at, nothing copied. 26 of 38 Steam achievements are hidden; all sit in the story chapter, though some with low unlock rates ("I Don't Got All Night" 3%, "Chatterbox" 3.2%, "Radical Acceptance" 4.1%, "One of the Thousand Young" 4.9%, "Nobody Knows What Happened" 5.5%) may be endings, second-character runs or side events. The setting words in the blurb come from RAWG's description.
